labels.notes: The label is not marked and the row stays partial, as the dispatch requires. I ran tools/ledger.py's docstring_label_re on text[:4000] and it finds nothing. The only bold-backticked token is the declaration name **`GX.troyanovTheorem_four_of_exists_gt_two_pi`** (char 766), which is house style and has no 'prefix:' part. The other bold text is the prose '**No label is marked here.**' (char 276). The label bullet is at char 309, unmarked, and cites `RamcovGX.tex:1930`, the \begin{cex} line. The quoted block matches l.1930 from 'Start from' to the displayed condition exactly once whitespace is normalised (script check). CHECKED (1): the restated Prop is GX.TroyanovTheorem. Probe /tmp/audit-tfour/Probe.lean imported GX.Spherical.TroyanovPolygon and GXScaffold.Spherical.TroyanovAngles and pasted the module source, so the module elaborated from source, with no name clash against TroyanovAngles. troyanovTheorem_of_five_le_of_exists_gt_two_pi has a non-dependent first binder (no loose bvars), and its conclusion is Expr-equal (==) and defeq to the value of GX.TroyanovTheorem (TroyanovAngles.lean:229-232, no universe parameters). `example (h : H5) : GX.TroyanovTheorem := GX.troyanovTheorem_of_five_le_of_exists_gt_two_pi h` typechecks. CHECKED (2): the s = 4 statements. I instantiated the value of TroyanovTheorem at s := 4 (mkNatLit 4) to get T4. The type of troyanovTheorem_four is Expr-equal to T4, so it covers every s = 4 datum. For troyanovTheorem_four_of_exists_gt_two_pi I telescoped three binders θ, hθ, hgt. hθ's type is Expr-equal to TroyanovAngleCondition θ. The body is Expr-equal to T4's body at θ, hθ and does not mention hgt. hgt's type is Expr-equal to the independently elaborated `∃ i, 2 * Real.pi < θ i`. So the hypotheses are exactly s = 4, TroyanovAngleCondition θ and some θ_i > 2π; θ_i ≠ 2π is not assumed. Also, `fun θ hθ => h θ hθ` turns a TroyanovTheorem h into the s = 4 statement. CHECKED (3): the s ≥ 5 reduction is an equivalence. The probe proved TroyanovTheorem ↔ (∀ s, 5 ≤ s → ∀ θ, TAC θ → (∀ i, θ i ≠ 2π) → (∃ i, 2π < θ i) → body). The forward direction is `fun h _ _ θ hθ _ _ => h θ hθ` and the backward one is the theorem. The remaining case is inhabited: the probe proved TAC, all ≠ 2π and some > 2π for (5π/2, 5π/2, 2π/5, 2π/5, 2π/5), where χ' = π/5. Both probe theorems use only the standard axioms. CHECKED (4): the hypotheses of exists_isConeSphere_dart against the condition. With α = θ'/2 and the angle above 2π at index 0, TAC gives: α_0 ∈ ]π, 2π[ (θ_0 < 4π: four_of_gt_two_pi); α_2 < π; α_0 + α_j < 2π (from Σ_{i≠l} θ_i ≤ 4π); χ' > 0 ⇔ Σα > 2π; χ' < 2θ_2, 2θ_3 ⇔ h013, h012; and α_2 + α_3 < 2π − α_0 < π < α_0 + α_1. I re-derived all of these by hand, and they match REPORT finding 3 and SCOPE (c). A second probe (Probe2) proved `exists_isConeSphere_dart` for α = (t0, t1, t2, t3)/2 from hypotheses that are symmetric in t1, t2, t3: positivity, χ' > 0, χ' ≤ t_j for j = 1, 2, 3, and t0 > 2π. This kernel-checks the REPORT's claim that any of the three other angles may sit opposite the reflex vertex. CHECKED (5): the cone angles, with no factor slip. DartParams.exists_isConeSphere concludes IsConeSphere M (fun i => 2 * D.α i) p. exists_dartParams returns D with D.α = α. troyanovTheorem_four_of_exists_gt_two_pi applies it at α = θ'/2, rewrites 2 * (θ' i / 2) = (θ ∘ σ) i, and undoes σ = swap 0 k with the strict IsConeSphere.comp_equiv (TroyanovPolygon.lean:108). So the angles are θ_i. That includes the reflex vertex: StarFrames.θc 0 = ⟨2α_0, _⟩ ∈ ]2π, 4π[, with the chart built on polarFold (α_0) and α_0 ∈ ]π, 2π[ allowed by StarFrames (α_pos, α_lt, α_ne). StarPolygon.isConeSphere fills the fields of the strict GX.IsConeSphere (ConeSurface.lean:958): homeomorphic is Homeomorph.refl Sph2, injective, pos, isConePoint i := ⟨coneXAChart i⟩, where coneXAChart is a strict XAChart SO3 Sph2 SphCone sphConeS (t.θc i) (vertex i), and sing_subset. The file defines no IsConePoint, IsConeSphere, XAChart, SO3 or Sph2. Its own types are StarFrames, StarPolygon, the synonym StarPolygon.Double := Sph2 and DartParams. The probe's statements, written with GX.SO3, GX.Sph2, GX.SingularGXStructure and GX.IsConeSphere from the strict imports, are Expr-equal to the theorems' types. The double's singular structure is the maximal a.e. atlas of the cone charts. Its compatibility is proved (isGXAtlas_atlas, through loc_up, loc_edge and loc_down), so is its portly support (isAEAtlas_atlas), as in the graduated TroyanovPolygon. The strict IsConePoint.angle_eq makes the angle unique. CHECKED (6): the IVT. At t = 0, T' is degenerate: dartFu = 1, because cos ε = cos²(ε/2) − sin²(ε/2). At t = 1, T' is a lune: dartFu = −1, because cos ε = cos(ε+δ)cos δ + sin(ε+δ)sin δ. In between, T stays strictly inside (−1, 1). Both formulas are the spherical law of cosines for angles, cos c = (cos C + cos A cos B)/(sin A sin B), with C = 2π − α_0 (so cos C = −cos ε) for T' and C = α_2 for T. The DartParams fields hT and hT' are the same law, rearranged. CHECKED (7): REPORT findings. None claims an error in the paper. (1) At s = 4 the printed condition is sufficient also with an angle above 2π. This is kernel-checked, the paper says only 'as long as', and 'nothing to change' stands. It does not touch OQ-59, which stays open. (2) The planner's 3 misses out of 3000 cannot be genuine non-existence: the dart exists for every datum (kernel-checked), and the planner's (Δ_2, Δ_4) dart is the same family, with Δ = p, q and u = Δ_2 − α. So 'resolution artefacts' is a fair reading, and it is a remark to the planner, not to the author. (3) The list of weaker hypotheses matches the Lean binders. (4) Non-vacuity is kernel-checked: (5π/2, π/2, 3π/5, 7π/10) has Σ = 43π/10 and χ' = 3π/10 ≤ π/2, with the angles pairwise distinct. I re-checked the arithmetic by hand. The REPORT's 'which machinery generalises' notes (1) and (2) agree with the code: StarFrames and StarPolygon are indexed by an arbitrary type, and isConeSphere by Fin s. Notes (3) to (5) are planning opinions and assert no theorem.

docstring_contract: The contract is lean-causal kb 0006, the one CAMPAIGN.md points to; lean-gx's own kb 0006 is the spherical-models entry. The docstring has, in order: the title; the label `cex:start_singular_manifold_homeomorphic` — `RamcovGX.tex:1930`, unmarked, at char 309; the quoted block (verbatim); an extra '## The construction' section (char 2552); '## Hypothesis checklist' (char 4197); '## SCOPE (disclosed)' (a)-(d) (char 4737); and the Provenance line (char 5469). All of them fall within the first 4000 characters, or follow them, as in the polygon module. The construction section is accurate, checked against the code. The condition gives α_0 + α_j + α_k ≤ 2π and Σα > 2π. The dart is T ∖ T' = {n₁ ≥ 0, n₂ ≥ 0} ∩ ({n₀ ≥ 0} ∪ {n₃ ≥ 0}), which is DartParams.P. I checked by hand that the far part of T's lune lies inside T''s lune, so the set is T ∖ int T'. The segment endpoints and the degenerations are as stated, and the angles of the dart are p − u = α_1, q − w = α_3, α_2, and 2π − (2π − α_0) = α_0. The SCOPE claims are true. (a): s = 4 only. (b): the cone point is IsConePoint's X_θ-chart. (c): the hypothesis list matches exists_isConeSphere_dart's binders, apart from the case assumptions α_0 ∈ ]π, 2π[ and α_i > 0; α_0 < 2π is redundant given h01. Necessity is not studied. (d): the Prop is restated inline (Expr-equal, CHECKED (1)), M : Type, and TroyanovAngles is not imported. Every Provenance cross-reference is used in the file: troyanovTheorem_of_exists_gt_two_pi, IsConeSphere.comp_equiv, SphPolygon.norm_le_of_gfun_nonneg, frameSO3, polarFold, isOpenMap_restrict_of_isCompact, symm_trans_mem_aeAtlas_of_opens, isPortly_compl_singleton_sph2, gaugeRescale and intermediate_value_Icc. Checklist rows 2, 4 and 5 are true. Row 1 has no symbol, as in TroyanovPolygon (not counted there either). Row 3 is the minor finding below. I do not count one trivial readability point. The module docstring's construction mixes the planner's base-point names v₂, v₄ with the 0-indexed apex v_2, and it calls the base L where the code uses 2ℓ. The DartParams docstring resolves this (v_1 = v₂, v_3 = v₄, base of length 2ℓ).

findings.what: Checklist row 3, 'the angles θ_i arbitrary | ✓ at s = 4, some θ_i > 2π (the case left by TroyanovPolygon)', puts the contract's ✓ (carried) on a restriction. The module's principal theorem, troyanovTheorem_four_of_exists_gt_two_pi, assumes some θ_i > 2π, which is more than 'arbitrary'. Only troyanovTheorem_four, which goes through TroyanovPolygon, carries every angle at s = 4. The text of the row is not false, and the restriction is disclosed in l.9-17, in row 1 and in SCOPE (a). The row is unmarked and partial. TroyanovPolygon's corresponding row used '⚠ restricted'.
